classification.difficultyReason: Derive the common ratio from square diagonals and apply the ninth-term formula.

content.prompt: A square has side length 1. A second square is then formed using the diagonal of the first square. A third square is then formed using the diagonal of the second square, and so on. Find the side length of the ninth square formed in this fashion.

spec.description: Three unfilled squares with a shared vertex: an upright unit square, a rotated intermediate square and a larger upright square. Red diagonals identify successive diagonal-to-side constructions; ordinary outlines are black.
spec.mathematics: The first square has side 1. Its diagonal is a side of the rotated square; the rotated square's vertical diagonal is the left side of the third square. Side lengths increase by a factor of sqrt(2).
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied unit-side label and construction are visible; the ninth side length is not shown.

answer.short:
$16$ units.

The side lengths form a geometric sequence with common ratio $\sqrt{2}$.
answer.worked:
A square of side length $s$ has diagonal $\sqrt{s^2+s^2}=s\sqrt{2}$. Hence the side lengths form a geometric sequence with first term $1$ and common ratio $\sqrt{2}$.

$$\begin{align*}a_n&=1\cdot(\sqrt{2})^{n-1}\\a_9&=(\sqrt{2})^8\\a_9&=2^4\\a_9&=16.\end{align*}$$

The ninth square has side length $16$ units.
